incident-bot: AUTOPAGE: PagerDuty incident fired for service=redwood-inference-canary test=canary-telemetry (severity=high)
pagerduty: Incident PD-89321 ➤ Trigger: canary error-rate > 3% over 5m (route: /v1/embed)
deploy-bot: release 2026-03-15T18:00:22 pushed to canary (sha: a1b2c3d). Canary started receiving 10% of traffic at 18:00 UTC.
jordan_oncall: ack — I got the page, jumping in. Anyone on the release?
sarah_release: oncall, that's our canary from the embed-quant rollout. I'm the release owner. seeing increased 502/504s and p99 latency spikes for embed calls.
mike_ops: confirming logs show repeated timeout errors from quant-node-3 and quant-node-7: `RPCError: upstream timeout` — looks like a kernel-level backpressure after token 512.
rebecca_sre: adding tracing link: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/trace/7f9c — the tail latencies line up with model shard handoff.
jordan_oncall: ok plan, let's reduce traffic to canary immediately and start rollback if mitigation doesn't cut errors in 3 mins. Can someone run the diversion?
sarah_release: doing traffic diversion now — switching traffic_split canary->0% via rollout API. CLI:```bash
curl -X POST https://platform.internal/api/rollouts/traffic -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"service":"embed","canary_pct":0}'
```
incident-bot: action accepted: traffic_split update queued (req id=0x7e4)
deploy-bot: traffic split update applied: canary=0% -> stable=100% (approx propagation 30s)
mike_ops: scaling up quant-pool to add headroom while we validate rollback: `kubectl scale --replicas=6 deploy/quant-node` — applied.
rebecca_sre: monitoring — error-rate down from 3.7% -> 0.6% in the last 60s; p95 embed latency trending down.
jordan_oncall: good. I'm going to clear the PagerDuty page if trend continues for another minute. Any customer-facing impact?
sarah_release: preliminary: small subset of customers (traffic routed to canary during 18:02-18:04) saw failed embedding requests, ~120 requests failed total across 6 orgs. No billing errors, just 5xxs. Will follow up with contact list.
mike_ops: capturing core dumps and svc logs to /var/reports/pd-89321/; grabbing kernel logs from quant-node-7.
sarah_release: we rolled canary back to stable snapshot (pre-quant-change). I'll open a bug and attach logs. Ticket: https://tickets.redwood/PD-89321-rollback created.
jordan_oncall: acked and resolved PD-89321 (manual resolve) — leaving thread for postmortem and customer comms. Thanks for the quick moves everyone. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PD-89321 marked resolved by jordan_oncall
sarah_release: short postmortem notes: cause likely quantized kernel path regression under long-context handoff; reproduction on canary under synthetic load — next steps: 1) disable quant-path by default on canary, 2) add guardrail to fail open to stable kernel on token > 256, 3) run extended soak on quant nodes.
rebecca_sre: assigning follow-ups: SRE to own soak validation (rebecca_sre), Release to own rollback postmortem + customer comms (sarah_release), Ops to do deeper kernel tracing (mike_ops).
mike_ops: attaching diagnostics: `/var/reports/pd-89321/diagnostics.zip` and snippet:```text
[quant-node-7] 18:03:12 ERR upstream timeout after 120000ms
[quant-node-7] 18:03:13 INFO kv-cache evicted prefix xyz
[quant-node-7] 18:03:14 CRIT unhandled exception in compute path
```
sarah_release: I'll draft customer notes and ping support to surface to impacted accounts. Anyone want to own comms?
jordan_oncall: I'll coordinate initial heads-up to account leads, cc: legal if needed.
rebecca_sre: creating a short RCA doc and scheduling follow-up 30-min triage in #incidents-postmortem at 19:00 UTC.
sarah_release: thanks all. leaving a reminder to not re-promote that quant build until kernel patches land.
pagerduty: automated follow-up: If any suppressed alerts remain, please reopen PD-89321 or create PD-XXXXX.
